newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Revamped Max sees swing back to profit.
newsitem.headline: Revamped Max sees swing back to profit.

text.p: Max Resources Ltd, which is transforming itself from an mineral prospecting firm into a waste processing company, had the suspension of trading in its shares lifted by the Stock Exchange on Monday.

The lifting came after Max provided financial forecasts which included a net loss of NZ$882,000 in the year to June 1997, followed by a net profit of $1.82 million in 1998 and a predicted $3.84 million in 1999.
The NZSE's Market Surveillance Panel had suspended Max from trading until it was satisfied that the market was being fairly informed.
In a statement the panel said it had approved the release of Max's forecasts relating to the firm's new business direction and therefore lifted the suspension.
"The panel is finalising its review of the circumstances surrounding these matters and will report its conclusion in the near future," it added.
Max will hold a shareholder meeting in late April or early May to approve the change of direction by acquiring various assets to manufacture and distribute organic fertiliser.
This meeting will consider the purchase of organic fertiliser-producing interests assets in the U.S., Indonesia, India, Sri Lanka and France.
